execution.mechanism: klt sim --backend batch (2am EDA batch fleet, Spot)
execution.timing_note: elapsed_s per corner is the remote engine wall clock reported by klt (runtime_s). job_elapsed_s is the fleet harness's own job time. queue_provision_and_transfer_s = submit-to-collect wall minus job_elapsed_s (S3 upload, Spot acquisition/boot, polling granularity, download).

experiment.claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Startup time' (< 1 ms), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Ramps the supply feeding design/bandgap_core.sch from 0 V to the corner supply in t_ramp and measures the first time VREF rises through 1.08 V (90% of the 1.20 V ratified nominal), open-circuit, over the full 45-point PVT matrix. NOTE: the core cell as merged by #8 contains no startup injector -- GDRV is exposed as the attachment node and the injector is issue #10's deliverable -- so this bench measures the core AS COMMITTED. A failure here is a statement about the missing injector, not about the bench.
experiment.title: Supply-ramp startup time of the untrimmed core over the full PVT matrix

spread_checks.note: The settled supply must move by at least 0.5 V across the matrix (2.97 -> 3.63 V is 0.66 V). This is the corner-liveness check for this bench: it proves the runner's supply knob reaches the simulator. It is deliberately NOT placed on t_start_ms or vref_final -- if the core does not self-start, those are pinned at their sentinel/zero values by the physics under test, and a spread check on them would report a second, redundant failure that says nothing new.
